Python Foundations Project: Austo¶

Problem Statement¶

Context¶

In the 21st century, cars are an important mode of transportation that provides us the opportunity for personal control and autonomy. In day-to-day life, people use cars for commuting to work, shopping, visiting family and friends, etc. Research shows that more than 76% of people prevent themselves from traveling somewhere if they don't have a car. Most people tend to buy different types of cars based on their day-to-day necessities and preferences. So, it is essential for automobile companies to analyze the preference of their customers before launching a car model into the market. Austo, a UK-based automobile company aspires to grow its business into the US market after successfully establishing its footprints in the European market.

In order to be familiar with the types of cars preferred by the customers and factors influencing the car purchase behavior in the US market, Austo has contracted a consulting firm. Based on various market surveys, the consulting firm has created a dataset of 3 major types of cars that are extensively used across the US market. They have collected various details of the car owners which can be analyzed to understand the automobile market of the US.

Objective¶

Austo's management team wants to understand the demand of the buyers and trends in the US market. They want to build customer profiles based on the analysis to identify new purchase opportunities so that they can manipulate the business strategy and production to meet certain demand levels. Further, the analysis will be a good way for management to understand the dynamics of a new market. Suppose you are a Data Scientist working at the consulting firm that has been contracted by Austo. You are given the task to create buyer's profiles for different types of cars with the available data as well as a set of recommendations for Austo. Perform the data analysis to generate useful insights that will help the automobile company to grow its business.

Data Description¶

austo_automobile.csv: The dataset contains buyer's data corresponding to different types of products(cars).

Data Dictionary¶

  • Age: Age of the customer
  • Gender: Gender of the customer
  • Profession: Indicates whether the customer is a salaried or business person
  • Marital_status: Marital status of the customer
  • Education: Refers to the highest level of education completed by the customer
  • No_of_dependents: Number of dependents(partner/children/spouse) of the customer
  • Personal_loan: Indicates whether the customer availed a personal loan or not
  • House_loan: Indicates whether the customer availed house loan or not
  • Partner_working: Indicates whether the customer's partner is working or not
  • Salary: Annual Salary of the customer
  • Partner_salary: Annual Salary of the customer's partner
  • Total_salary: Annual household income (Salary + Partner_salary) of the customer's family
  • Price: Price of the car
  • Make: Car type (Hatchback/Sedan/SUV)

# Function to plot histograms and boxplots for numerical variables
def univariate_num(data, col, title):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

    # Histogram
    sns.histplot(data=data, x=col, kde=True, ax=ax[0], color='teal')
    ax[0].set_title(f'Distribution of {title}')

    # Boxplot
    sns.boxplot(data=data, x=col, ax=ax[1], color='orange')
    ax[1].set_title(f'Boxplot of {title}')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Function to plot countplots for categorical variables
def univariate_cat(data, col, title):
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    ax = sns.countplot(data=data, x=col, palette='viridis', order=data[col].value_counts().index)
    plt.title(f'Count of {title}')

    # Add percentage labels
    total = len(data)
    for p in ax.patches:
        percentage = f'{100 * p.get_height() / total:.1f}%'
        x = p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2 - 0.05
        y = p.get_height()
        ax.annotate(percentage, (x, y), ha='center', va='bottom')
    plt.show()

[Q6] Numerical Variables Analysis

Observations:¶

  1. Age Distribution:

    • The age distribution is slightly right-skewed with a prominent peak between 25 and 35 years. This confirms that Austo's primary customer base is young working professionals.
    • The median age appears to be around 30, with very few customers above 50.

  2. Price Structure (Multimodal):

    • The Price histogram shows three distinct peaks (Multimodal distribution).
    • These peaks clearly correspond to the three car segments:
      • Peak 1 (~$20k): Likely Hatchbacks.
      • Peak 2 (~$35k-$45k): Likely Sedans.
      • Peak 3 (~$60k+): Likely SUVs.
    • This suggests clear product segmentation with little pricing overlap.

  3. Salary & Income:

    • Salary: Right-skewed distribution. Most individual customers earn between $40k and $80k.
    • Total Salary: Shows a wider spread. The upper tail indicates a segment of high-household-income buyers who are the likely target for the premium SUV segment.

Observations:¶

  1. Demographics (Target Audience):

    • Gender: Heavily skewed towards Males (approx. 75%).
    • Marital Status: Overwhelmingly Married (approx. 90%).
    • Implication: The core customer is a married male. Marketing should heavily emphasize family-oriented features (Safety ratings, trunk space, ISOFIX child seat mounts).

  2. Profession & Education:

    • Profession: Fairly balanced, with 'Salaried' ~55% slightly edging out 'Business' ~45%

    • Education: The vast majority are Post-Graduates, indicating a highly educated, white-collar customer base.

  3. Car Make (Market Demand):

    • Sedans are the volume leader ~700 units, followed closely by Hatchbacks ~600 units.
    • SUVs are a smaller segment (~300 units), likely due to their higher price point (as seen in Q6). They represent the "Premium/Niche" market rather than mass market.

  4. Financial Behavior (Loans):

    • Personal Loan: Surprisingly high uptake (~50% of customers have a personal loan).
    • House Loan: A significant portion also have house loans.
    • Implication: The customer base is comfortable with debt. Aggressive financing offers (e.g., "Zero Down Payment" or "Low APR") would likely be very effective conversion tools.

  1. Premium Segment Discovery: Surprisingly, 50.23% (444 out of 884) of Hatchbacks are priced above $25,000.

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 12: Write the conclusions and business recommendations derived from the analysis. (6 marks)¶

A. Market Segmentation & Buyer Profiles¶

  1. The "Premium Hatchback" Opportunity (Based on Q7):

    • Insight: 50.23% of Hatchback sales are >$25k. This is a massive, premium sub-segment.
    • Strategy: Do not market Hatchbacks as "Cheap." Launch a specific "Sport/Lux" Hatchback trim to cater to this 50%. Feature-led marketing (Sunroof, Tech) will work better than Price-led marketing here.
    • Action Item: Create two distinct brochure types for Hatchbacks: "Efficiency" (for the <$25k segment) and "Performance" (for the >$25k segment).

  2. The High-Value Salaried Professional (Based on Q10 & Q11):

    • Insight: Across key segments (Small Family, High Debt), Salaried professionals consistently outspend Business owners (by ~$2k - $4k).
    • Profile: Likely corporate employees who view cars as status symbols and are comfortable with monthly payments (EMI).
    • Strategy: They are the primary target for Up-selling. Pitch them the "Top Model" Sedan or SUV. They are less price-sensitive than Business owners in comparable situations.

  3. The Practical Business Buyer (Based on Q10):

    • Insight: Business owners spending less (~$32k) suggests a focus on utility or cost-consciousness in this dataset.
    • Strategy: Pitch "Value," "Low Maintenance," and "Durability" to the Business segment. Highlight "Total Cost of Ownership" rather than monthly EMI.

B. Financing Strategy¶

  1. Leveraging Debt Comfort (Based on Q8 & Q11):
    • Insight: Salaried employees maintain high spending even with loans. 46% of high-spenders take loans.
    • Action: Launch "Consolidated EMI" plans. Since they likely have other loans, offer a car loan structure that starts low and increases (Step-up EMI) to fit their cash flow.

C. Portfolio & Customer Lifecycle¶

  1. Inventory Planning:

    • Stock Depth: Ensure high availability of Mid-to-High trim Sedans for the Salaried class.
    • SUVs: Keep as the niche flagship (only ~20% of market), targeting the ultra-high income bracket (Total Salary >$100k) identified in Q9.

  2. Lifecycle Management (The "Austo Upgrade" Path):

    • Insight: The clear age progression (Hatchback -> Sedan -> SUV) is a retention goldmine.
    • Action: Implement a 3-Year Upgrade Program. Target Hatchback buyers (Median age 28) with guaranteed buyback offers when they hit age 31-32 (the typical Sedan entry age), making it seamless for them to trade in their Hatchback for a new Austo Sedan.

D. Marketing Channels¶

  1. Channel Mix:
    • Digital (Instagram/TikTok): Focus exclusively on the Entry-Level Hatchback ($15k-$25k) targeting the <30 demographic.
    • LinkedIn: The primary channel for the Premium Salaried segment ($35k+). Advertise "Executive Sedans" and "Status" here.
    • Local Business Forums: Target the Business segment with "Fleet/Utility" offers focusing on depreciation benefits.
